question: Explain one reported empirical finding with its metric and scope, and distinguish it from hypothesised applications.

u638d145f43da593f92c7.quote: Expert scientists excel at weighing empirical findings from multiple sources that vary in both statistical reliability and epistemic relevance. To what extent are language models, which are increasingly driving autonomous discovery systems, capable of such evidence deliberation? We introduce EDB-Bio, a scientific reasoning benchmark curated from real-world data in three biological domains: drug-perturbation transcriptomics, CRISPR screens, and human genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Each of EDB-Bio's 96k episodes presents a sequence of experimental results from published studies and asks the model to predict the probability that a target hypothesis is true. Out-of-the-box, open-weight and frontier models alike demonstrate systematic underconfidence and attain Brier scores comparable to a trivial base-rate forecaster. Post-training against strictly proper scoring rules significantly improves both calibration and discrimination. This calibration pays off downstream: in a sequential experiment selection task, our Ibis0 model is 2.5 times more efficient than the best frontier model. Throughout, quantifying evidence weights as Bayes factors reveals how models update their beliefs over time, whether they agree with expert biologists on relevance, and where they exhibit inconsistencies and biases. Our work extends calibration training and uncertainty analysis to a realistic scientific forecasting setting with applications to human cancer biology. We release all code, data, and trained models.

exact_initial_request_context.comparison_contract: Coverage is the single authoritative mapping. Do not emit comparison_claims or comparison_basis. An answer reference for a comparison must be an actual comparative finding with separately cited evidence handles from all necessary sources. Qualitative method contrasts require supported method descriptions, not necessarily common benchmarks. Empirical performance conclusions require compatible evaluation tasks, comparators, metric definitions and conditions. Source notes stay context if the requested comparison is unanswered; partial retains every gap and earns no full answer credit. Support, atomicity, qualifications and actual request relevance are checked independently.
exact_initial_request_context.coverage_wire_rule: Coverage alone maps sealed requested parts to emitted answer/context claim IDs. No claims.part_ids, missing/orphan/duplicate/overlapping references. Full abstention omits claims and ALL claim references. A comparison answer needs independently cited source bases; comparison-only notes leave the requested comparison unanswered.
exact_initial_request_context.identity_contract: Emit only actual claims in order. Server assigns c1,c2 and later positions. Coverage is the only answer/context mapping: exactly each required named part, all genuine gap reasons. Questions distinguish context_claim_ids (topic links, no factual premise) from premise_claim_ids (investigate_claim only, independently checked). The structural answer tag grants no full-answer credit.

abstention.application_context_required: I cannot assess the requested application without further context and evidence.
abstention.comparison_evidence_required: I cannot establish the requested comparison from the selected evidence.
abstention.insufficient_selected_evidence: I cannot establish the requested conclusion from the selected evidence.

actions.inspect_evaluation: Inspect evaluation methods, baselines and uncertainty before drawing conclusions.
actions.inspect_methods: Inspect the original methods and implementation details.
actions.inspect_scope: Check source scope and applicability before proposing an experiment.
actions.request_context: Request the missing source material or application context.
actions.seek_counterevidence: Seek evidence that could challenge the cited claims.

questions.application_scope: Does the selected evidence establish applicability to the proposed setting?
questions.counterevidence: What evidence could challenge the cited claims?
questions.implementation: What further evidence would be needed to implement or reproduce the method?
questions.investigate_claim: What evidence supports or limits the referenced claim?
questions.measured_and_proposed: Which claims report measured results, and what applications, if any, does the excerpt propose?
questions.methods: What methods, if any, does the selected evidence describe?
questions.qualifications: What assumptions or qualifications, if any, apply to the cited claims?

procedural_rendering.rule: Neutral intents may have context_claim_ids but no premise_claim_ids. investigate_claim requires nonempty premise_claim_ids; never introduce an assertion outside the scored claims.

exact_initial_request_context.request_quality_rule: At most 8 atomic claims in learn mode; about 500 characters per claim and 240 per explanation are SOFT targets only. Preserve qualifications rather than shortening into misleading claims. Record every requested part exactly once as answered, partial, lacks_evidence or omitted. Available but unreported information is omitted. Context notes do not answer a comparison. All semantic quality and factual prose remain reviewed. Partial requires useful answer refs AND genuine remaining gaps; answered requires no remaining gap. Context alone never earns answer credit.
